text: This issue is meant to track all issues and features around managing GPUs in kubernetes. This issue is meant to reflect priorities, timeline and owners too. ## v1.7 - [x] All GPUs get exposed to privileged containers #46007 [Owner: @cmluciano, Reviewer: @vishh ] - kubernetes/kubernetes.github.io#3870 - [x] Enable GPU node e2e tests - Requires starting VMs in GCE with GPUs [ Owner: @vishh ] #45430 - [x] Enable Cluster e2e tests - Requires automated installation of Nvidia drivers on COS image [ @vishh] #45136 ## Post v1.7 (1.8) - [ ] Avoid depending of docker APIs for identifying GPUs in Use. Fixing this issue will make GPU integration work with all runtimes #43240 [Owner: @jiayingz, Reviewer: @vishh ] - [ ] Add GPU metrics to cadvisor - [ ] Run GPU e2e on PRs #47192 ## Known Bugs - [ ] Support for hot-plug of GPUs #44080 (Dropped because Nvidia drivers recommend rebooting nodes post installation) - [x] gpusInUse info error when kubelet restarts #46087 --- I'd like to add [NVML support](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/pull/414) to this list I'm also working on some of the [TODOs in the NVIDIA pkg](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/43240) @cmluciano I'd prefer not tackling NVML until the overall integration for GPUs is finalized. Meanwhile, we can address all other open issues and improve testing, etc. xref: #44552 I prepared a proposal for what we call the [Container Device Interface (CDI)](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/pull/545): A generic way to allocate devices, including GPUs, to containers. ---- We use Kubernetes to schedule scientific 3D visualisation applications onto a cluster. Hence our containers use GPUs / DRM and other device nodes (e.g. TTYs). Scheduling of Pods to Nodes with a capacity for such devices can be dealt with using [Opaque Integer Resources (OIR)](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-compute-resources-container/#opaque-integer-resources-alpha-feature), where scripts external to Kubernetes handle device discovery and capacity reporting (see e.g. [kube-gpu-resources](https://github.com/urzds/kube-gpu-resources)). The [Container Runtime Interface (CRI)](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/container-runtime-interface.md) already supports [binding host device nodes](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/api/v1alpha1/runtime/api.proto#L586) to a container. What is currently missing is a way for the Kubelet to generically allocate the available devices of a certain type to a container while it is being started. The Container Device Interface (CDI) shall bridge this gap. ---- Please find the [full text of the proposal](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/pull/545) in our copy of the Kubernetes proposal documents. I don't believe that this is a feature that we are targeting since I am not aware of wide-spread support of shared cards. cc @flx42 @renaudwastaken All Nvidia cards support sharing. Some (=recent ones) better than others. We have been sharing them for the past three years in our environment and for more than an year under Kubernetes, starting from G2 (Kepler-class) instances. There's an undocumented hack in pre-1.6 versions, but with recent ones you need ugly patching. I brought it up in the past, but it's already difficult enough to find an agreement on more basic stuff like discovery. It is doable, but you'd need to bring a lot more state and GPU awareness into the Kubernetes scheduler (or use a separate one). I also mentioned this before, but I'll re-iterate: there is no enforced isolation between computation kernels on the GPU. You should share the hardware only if you know what you are doing and/or trust what you are running. By default, kernels from different processes can't run on one GPU **simultaneously** (concurrency but not parallelism), they are time sliced. The Pascal architecture brings instruction-level preemption instead of block-level preemption, but context switches are not free. Also, there is no way of partitioning GPU resources (SMs, memory), or even assignin priorities when sharing a card. I agree with @therc that there is higher priority work before considering GPU sharing. For our usecase (multiple different Neural networks being evaluated in different containers) all the restrictions you stated would be fine. title: Federated tests should retry NodePort allocation
text:
In order to support running tests in parallel, we added randomized NodePort selection.  There appears to be some evidence that this is not sufficient and is causing e2e test flakes:

I already check the current code, and propose to retry the service creation until success or all possible ports (between FederatedSvcNodePortFirst and FederatedSvcNodePortLast) have been tried.

If this approach is fine for you, I can submit a PR soon.

How do you plan to check if the NodePorts are available? In our presubmit test environment, tests run across many instances of federation control planes in parallel, but share the same underlying clusters. So this approach might be viable depending on how and where you plan to check for these used NodePorts.

my approach for getting an available port is a "Dummy" approach: create a list of possible available port, get one of them randomly, then try to create the Service. If Service creation failed. try to use another possible available port, until service creation success or all possible available ports have been tested.

Sounds reasonable to me. Go for it.

A couple of caveats: 
1. No need to create a real list, you could just use the range boundaries. 
2. Be careful about service creation failure. You need to check if the service shard creation failed in the underlying clusters and rollback all those shards before retrying.

@madhusudancs thanks for the caveats, I will do soon a PR.

title: Tag e2e tests for alpha features as such and exclude them as appropriate from upgrade testing
text: Currently, there is no explicit tagging of e2e tests that exercise alpha features. Because we provide no guarantees for compatibility across k8s versions for these features, these tests frequently fail in our upgrade jobs when running some form of version-skewed testing (i.e. create a 1.5 cluster, upgrade the master to 1.6, run 1.5 E2E tests against the cluster). We should tag any e2e tests for alpha features as such, and explicitly exclude these from the relevant upgrade test jobs to eliminate noise in the release cycles. This will require ongoing maintenance to adjust the tags on the tests as a feature moves from alpha to beta to GA. cc @timothysc @ethernetdan @marun --- Some of the root causes around failures in some of the upgrade tests were breaking compat behavior from Alpha-Beta. Perhaps it would be easier to just skip [Alpha] tests as part of upgrade, b/c we make no guarantees across releases.?.? /cc @kubernetes/sig-scheduling-bugs @derekwaynecarr +1 There are alpha features known to be incompatible. If we see failures caused by such incompatibilities, we should skip the upgrade tests. The question is that "can we find a solution, such as versioning, etc., to automatically or semi-automatically detect these incompatibilities?" By semi-automatically I mean something along the lines of tagging all the tests with the features that they test. This needs to be done once. Then we can have a master config which lists all the features. We can mark which features we expect to break in the latest upgrade. We may want to have multiple of these master configs, each for upgrading from a specific version to another. The benefit of this is that we won't need to tag tests again and again for every upgrade. Of course, all of these are just raw ideas that came to my mind as I was typing this message. If you think there is value, we can explore this more. > The question is that "can we find a solution, such as versioning, etc., to automatically or semi-automatically detect these incompatibilities?" yes, just add [Alpha] to tests the exercise alpha features and add it to the ginkgo skip list. > yes, just add [Alpha] to tests the exercise alpha features and add it to the ginkgo skip list. Sure, but as skriss said, that would require ongoing maintenance to adjust the tags in the future. As long as it makes it into the general alpha => beta checklist, it seems pretty manageable. I don't see why we can't add this logic in 1.7. I think manually tagging is fine. But I am not sure alpha always implies we break compatibility. It just means we MIGHT break compatibility. For example, 1.5 affinity test would work against 1.6 cluster, except for the fact that we flag-gated the 1.5 behavior in 1.6 and disabled it by default, which for some other features in the future (especially ones that are not using annotations in alpha) we might not do. So I would suggest the tag say something more specific than just "alpha" -- it should imply alpha and not expected to work in next version. > But I am not sure alpha always implies we break compatibility. It just means we MIGHT break compatibility. It means we guarantee nothing so the tests should not be trusted outside of a release. I think the smallest repro case I've seen so far is the one @r2d4 put together in [this comment on minikube issue #1252](https://github.com/kubernetes/minikube/issues/1252#issuecomment-295370860). I think this comes from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/44507, also https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/39816 TPRs never get registered with RegisterGroup (should they?), and the garbage collector controller as well as the namespace controller both use static RESTMapping, rather than a dynamic one. The versions get enabled and registered, but the group does not get registered causing the panic here: https://github.com/kubernetes/apimachinery/blob/master/pkg/apimachinery/registered/registered.go#L285 When I registered the group TPR, the panics disappear since the controllers know about the mappings, however the garbage collector complains since it doesn't know how to garbage collect the TPR. Right now the garbage collector suppresses some TPR errors https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/42862 One other possible fix is to ignore enable versions which don't map to a corresponding GroupMeta. Probably not a great solution, but would fix this problem for us until we get dynamic RESTMappings in the garbage and namespace controllers Not super familiar with this part of k8s so feel free to correct me or point me in the right direction. FYI I couldn't reproduce this in a full cluster (without minikube) on GCE with a method similar to https://github.com/kubernetes/minikube/issues/1252#issuecomment-295370860. I brought up the cluster, created the TPR, then "upgraded" the master to the same version, which removes and recreates the master VM while keeping the data volume intact. The TPR is still there, and I don't see any panics. title: Role/ClusterRole creation doesn't cross authorizers nicely
text:
In order to create an RBAC role, I need to have all of the permissions that exist in the role, *through RBAC*. It doesn't matter If I have all the permissions through another authorizer.

On GKE, for example, if I want to use my Google identity to create a role, I first have to create an RBAC RoleBinding giving myself the `cluster-admin` role, even if I am the owner of the project that has the GKE cluster.

We should authorize role creation in a way that allows "super users" from other authorizers to use RBAC.

---

Cc @kubernetes/sig-auth-feature-requests 

As a workaround, a GKE cluster admin can grant themselves RBAC permissions first:
```
kubectl create clusterrolebinding i-am-root --clusterrole=cluster-admin --user=<myusername>
```

Another check like this? https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/39383

I was thinking something similar to that.

Strawman:
To see if a user should be able to create/update a clusterRole:
Check "clusterRoleBindings" "bind" on the root of the cluster.
To see if a user should be able to create/update a role:
Check "roleBindings" "bind" on the whole namespace.

If you can bind to any existing role/clusterRole, then you can create/update roles/clusterRoles.

I think this is reasonable if you assume there is always a superuser role in every context. It might fall over if you consider a namespace that only has some low privilege roles that you are now able to escalate.

title: Lost Chat
text:
Type: Bug I'm new to using VSC. Today is Day 0. I was in the middle of the setup / configuration steps when I clicked on the menu at the left of my screen to see what the icon would do. My prompt window disappeared and the only prompt window I could get back was blank. There was no history to be found anywhere using the icons and menus in the app. I turned to Perplexity and explained the issue. Perplexity guided me through the steps to see if I could find it and I discovered there might be a bug in the Mac version of the VSC app. When I click on the Explorer icon in the upper left corner of my screen on the menu side bar, the folder tree was completely blank. I had already gotten through the step that created a new folder structure on my computer and I could see that folder structure physically with contents inside some of the folders, but it wasn't appearing within the tree of the Explorer icon so the app treated it as if it didn't exist. I ended up recovering the work and picked up where I left off, by using a prompt in the VSC chat window. Here's my prompt: "I lost where we left off on the demo project. Please search my computer for the MD file and folder structure we created earlier today and pick up where we left off." Claude came back with a bunch of Bash commands which I had to approve, and was able to locate the information that was indeed, still available to the system and I was able to recover the work. It was all still there, but just not visible on the side bar menu. I have since been able to work to build that missing tree structure so I can come back later and find the same chat stream since I'm not finished with my project. title: Add Alt+click to close other tabs (JetBrains-style)
text: ## Feature Request Close all other tabs (except the current one) by _alt + clicking_ an editor tab's close button. By holding _alt_ over a tab's close button, the button swaps from the "Close" icon to a "Close Other Editors" icon. Clicking it closes all other tabs in the group, leaving the clicked tab open. **Note:** If there was an open sticky tab, it stays unchanged. This is the same behavior as JetBrains IDEs ([docs](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/mps/closing-files-in-the-editor.html)). ### Implementation PR: #328975 --- This is actually better than JetBrains, as their tooltip is static (doesn't change if _alt_ is pressed) and it shows the tips for both _Close_ and _Close Others_, making the tooltip polluted. Sharing media and context from merged PR #328975 for verification: # Add Alt+click to close other tabs (JetBrains-style) Close all other tabs (except the current one) by _alt + clicking_ an editor tab's close button. By holding _alt_ over an editor tab's close button, the button swaps from the "Close" icon to a "Close Other Editors" icon. Clicking it closes every other non-sticky tab in the group, leaving the clicked tab (and any sticky tabs) open. This is the same behavior as JetBrains IDEs ([docs](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/mps/closing-files-in-the-editor.html)). ## Demo ## Edge case: tabs whose `matches()` is intentionally loose Some editor inputs (e.g. `GettingStartedInput`, used for Welcome and walkthrough tabs) override `matches()` to return `true` for any instance of the same type, so VS Code can treat them as a reusable singleton pane elsewhere. Using `matches()` to decide what "close others" should close meant that if two such tabs were open together, alt + clicking one would incorrectly spare the other instead of closing it. The close filter compares by reference identity instead, since what matters here is "is this literally the tab that was clicked," not "is this the same kind of tab." ## Known limitation **Pre-existing, not introduced by this PR**, `workbench.action.closeOtherEditors` already has the identical exposure today. If two same type loosely-matching tabs (e.g. two `GettingStartedInput` tabs) are open in one group and the clicked tab is active, _closing others_ can close the wrong one.

Needs a separate PR to fix it. ## How to test 1. Open several tabs (leave at least one pinned/sticky, if you'd like to check that case too) 2. Hover a non-sticky tab's close (×) button and hold _alt_: the icon swaps to "Close Other Editors" 3. Click it while _alt_ is held 4. Expect: every other non-sticky tab closes; sticky tabs and the clicked tab remain open 5. Release _alt_ without clicking: the icon reverts to the plain Close (×) 6. Hold _alt_ over a sticky tab's Unpin button: it should stay Unpin, unaffected by Alt ## Test coverage `multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts` (real `MultiEditorTabsControl` + DOM + `EditorGroupModel`): - Shows Close by default, swaps to Close Other Editors while Alt is held, reverts on release - Sticky tabs keep showing Unpin regardless of Alt - Clicking while Alt is held closes every other non-sticky tab - Handles the `matches()` edge case above - Clicking a sticky tab's Unpin button while Alt is held does not close other tabs - Without Alt, clicking closes only that one tab `editorActions.test.ts` (`CloseOtherEditorTabsInGroupAction` in isolation): - Closes every other editor, keeping the target by reference - Keys off identity, not `matches()`, so a loosely-matching editor doesn't wrongly spare the target - Does nothing if the group referenced in context can't be resolved the setting is off Source PR: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328975

text: Tracking issue for the Voice Mode ambient glow redesign. | PR | Scope | Status | | --- | --- | --- | | https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328455 | The rim redesign across the chat inputs | Merged | | https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328484 | Dictation mic glow uniformity | In review | Voice Mode's ambient glow is currently a hardcoded blue/purple border plus box-shadow, applied identically on every surface. title: Extension host terminated unexpectedly 3 times within the last 5 minutes.
text:
- VS Code Version: 1.132.0
- OS Version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200

Behaviour:
I have started to encounter this error since 1.126.0. Each time I open vs code it says Extension host terminated unexpectedly. I tried  `code --disable-extensions` and disable all the extensions but still got this error. I'm still using 1.125.0 as this version works fine. I'm in china and not sure if this is related. 


---

Can you share crash dump following https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Native-Crash-Issues#creating-a-crash-report to vscode-logs@microsoft.com

Thanks for replying. Just shared. I'll also share the report here. 

[reports.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30962975/reports.zip)

## AI Analysis
I analyzed all three dumps in the attached `reports.zip`. They have the same native crash signature:

```text
Process: node.mojom.NodeService (the local extension host utility process)
Crash reason: EXCEPTION_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION (0xC000001D)
Faulting module: C:\Windows\System32\ASProxy64.dll
Fault address: ASProxy64.dll + 0xc274
ASProxy64.dll version: 2.3.6.3

Stack prefix:
  ASProxy64.dll + 0xc274
  ASProxy64.dll + 0x1f4c2
  ASProxy64.dll + 0x65ec8
  ASProxy64.dll + 0xc506
  ASProxy64.dll + 0x1f8ad
  runtime.node
```

`ASProxy64.dll` is Astrill VPN's proxy/LSP DLL. It is injected into the extension-host process and executes the illegal instruction that terminates it. Because this is a system-wide Winsock provider, exiting Astrill or starting VS Code with `--disable-extensions` does not necessarily stop the DLL from loading.

This is the same faulting DLL, exception, and `+0xc274` stack signature previously investigated in #325035. In that report, properly cleaning up the Astrill/ASProxy installation resolved the crash.

The reported 1.125 -> 1.126 boundary does not coincide with an Electron target change: both releases use Electron target 42.3.0. The bundled Copilot extension and its native runtime did change between those releases (`@github/copilot` 1.0.61 -> 1.0.64-0). The dump returns from Astrill code into Copilot's `runtime.node`, so changed startup/network activity may have exposed the existing Astrill incompatibility, but the instruction that actually faults belongs to `ASProxy64.dll`.

Recommended remediation:

1. Update Astrill to its latest available version.
2. Properly unregister Astrill's LSP: hold **Ctrl**, open Astrill's **Help** menu, and select **Uninstall LSP**.
3. Log out of and close Astrill, then restart Windows.
4. If the LSP must remain installed, try excluding `Code.exe` using Astrill's Application Filter.
5. Avoid only deleting or renaming `ASProxy64.dll`; the Winsock provider should be properly unregistered to remove all traces safely.

No VS Code code change is indicated by these dumps. I am leaving this issue open for confirmation that unregistering/updating Astrill resolves it on the affected machine.

It worked! thank you!

title: Space should not delete files on macOS when closing unsaved work
text: validated this based on actually watching and interacting with the noted test behaviors. I had two sessions one pointing at vscode and one at electron both with this issue as context and the idea about looking into exposing the destructive flag as possibly a thing as well as understanding why this is weird in sequoia. The root TLDR cause on this is vscode button order shuffling - don't save is the last button to be added, so it gets keyboard focus. --- I dug further into the native path. One useful distinction is that **Save is still the default button** here: Return activates Save. **Don't Save has keyboard focus**, so Space activates it when macOS Keyboard Navigation is enabled. VS Code currently changes the logical order `[Save, Don't Save, Cancel]` into the native insertion order `[Save, Cancel, Don't Save]`. Electron then creates an `NSAlert`, assigns Return and Escape using `defaultId`/`cancelId`, but otherwise leaves AppKit to choose the initial first responder. On Sequoia 15.7.7, an isolated AppKit test reproduced the result: that VS Code insertion order initially focuses Don't Save. Preserving `[Save, Don't Save, Cancel]` instead initially focuses Cancel, so removing VS Code's legacy macOS button shuffle appears to be the smallest immediate fix. Separately, Electron currently has no message-box option corresponding to `NSButton.hasDestructiveAction`. Testing that property with the existing VS Code order also moved initial focus from Don't Save to Cancel. Adding such an Electron option would be the more explicit long-term solution, including destructive appearance and AppKit semantics, but it isn't required for the narrow ordering fix. Verified in latest insiders: With Keyboard navigation ON, "Cancel" is the default selected now (does not delete the files). With Keyboard navigation OFF, "Save" is the default on "Enter". thanks for the fix - can confirm all good now in release version. I understand the sentiment, and this is arguably a sane default. Is there any way we could make this configurable though? I often keep various unsaved "scratch" documents and use keyboard navigation to close them quickly when e.g. "Closing all to the right". It's a shortcut I use multiple times a day and was frustrated to find gone. text: with dialogs when closing the app / a file. I suspect that you won't find many where spacebar is destructive. But the answer to this has a good technical path to solve your simple keystroke ideal here (which I want too). Implement hasDestructiveAction in electron, and add Cmd+Delete as the keyboard shortcut for don't save. Probably the latter can be done already. The former is not too hard either, but requires enough coordination of pieces that I didn't want to throw some LLM slop at this. > However I think the measure of whether it's good or not has to come from what harm does it prevent. It's a fine position but I don't believe it's definitive. My view of keyboard navigation in macOS is that Enter triggers the primary/blue thing of the dialog, Escape closes doing nothing, and Space trigger the first other option. The whole point of keyboard navigation is to have an extra alternative outlined. If you don't want keyboard navigation, you don't have to enable it. > Another evaluation lens might be to look for other macOS native apps (as opposed to electron stuff) that seems to do the right thing with dialogs when closing the app / a file. I suspect that you won't find many where spacebar is destructive. I just tried out SublimeText which is the other tabbed editor I have : The Pages/Numbers apps examples are not the same kind of dialog. If I press Enter in our dialog, then I get a similar one. And indeed the first alternative input is selected and space writes in it. But Space does not trigger cancel here either. Adding my voice to ask for making this configurable at least. It should be easy to close a scratch editor and dismiss its contents. `Cmd+W, Space` was perfect for that. I think this change is overly cautious and making a perfectly normal workflow unnecessarily complicated. Also, please keep in mind that in order for the space key to do anything in this situation, Keyboard navigation has to be turned on in the macOS system preferences as shown in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/325273#issuecomment-5052743766, so this is automatically a power user feature.

Note that this is just a workaround, since it does not fix the actual issue of `Y` being responded to any message, but rather disables the autoresponse alltogether I bet this is conpty reprinting causing duplicate responses 🤦 Updating to Windows 11 might workaround this as I've never hit this issue. The theory is that something running in the terminal is triggering conpty (the backend component) to reprint the screen which would re-output the match text. These machines are ones where GPU acceleration doesn't work and we fallback to the DOM 2. Webgl init throws [here](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/blob/d81b25c3bf6c0e3352c175705f460aa39df6e374/addons/addon-webgl/src/WebglRenderer.ts#L101-L104) which disables it 3. But it doesn't appear that we clean up listeners created earlier, so [this listener](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/blob/d81b25c3bf6c0e3352c175705f460aa39df6e374/addons/addon-webgl/src/WebglRenderer.ts#L92) ends up firing shortly afterwards which causes the texture atlas to get created and warmed up. This operating is either totally broken or impossibly slow with this setup which causes the problem. So the fix I think is to make sure any listener in `WebglRenderer`'s ctor is disposed if it throws. I think this was caused because we previously detected such systems and removed it as it was thought we no longer needed that check in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/236276. We may want to bring that back (@deepak1556?), but I believe the change above should fix the problem. @Tyriar the fix you are proposing seems the better option, the previous check we had only tested for swiftshader backend and the reports I got so far don't seem to have that. @Ratstail91 @wgroh quick follow-up on your side, 1) Run `Developer: Toggle Developer Tools` 2) run the following snippet ``` const c = document.createElement('canvas') c.getContext('webgl2') ``` do you get `null` as the output ? Thanks For Fixing :) This Error But Till When It Will Be Fixed Properly ???? @deepak1556 ``` canvas : canvas drawingBufferColorSpace : "srgb" drawingBufferFormat : 32856 drawingBufferHeight : 150 drawingBufferWidth : 300

title: add support in omni-chat to run vscode commands
text: Adding to our initial LLM call which determines whether to route the request to a new session or to an existing one, we'd want to detect if a VS Code command can handle the request. Then, we'd add a new looking mode where we display the command that's getting run with a 10 second time out to cancel it. --- Sharing media and context from merged PR #330025 for verification: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf215eed-072e-40bb-925d-f5149b6e5896 ## Summary - add a first-stage command-vs-chat intent decision to omni-chat routing - restrict command routing to a curated set of reversible built-in VS Code UI commands - shortlist and classify commands using localized command titles only; command IDs are never sent to the model - deterministically recognize common directives such as `toggle terminal`, `toggle panel`, and `change VS Code theme` - show a 5-second `Running command X` review state with Run Now, Send to Chat, and Cancel actions - focus the invoking workbench window before revalidating and executing the command - preserve explicit new-session and pending voice-reply routing - use a 5-second session-routing countdown, retaining 10 seconds for multi-root workspaces where folder selection may require more time ## Commands eligible for execution Only the following currently enabled built-in commands are considered. All other built-in and extension commands continue through chat/session routing. ### Views and layout - Focus Panel (`workbench.action.focusPanel`) - Focus Primary Side Bar (`workbench.action.focusSideBar`) - Focus Secondary Side Bar (`workbench.action.focusAuxiliaryBar`) - Toggle Panel (`workbench.action.togglePanel`) - Toggle Primary Side Bar (`workbench.action.toggleSidebarVisibility`) - Toggle Secondary Side Bar (`workbench.action.toggleAuxiliaryBar`) - Toggle Terminal (`workbench.action.terminal.toggleTerminal`) - Toggle Zen Mode (`workbench.action.toggleZenMode`) - Toggle Full Screen (`workbench.action.toggleFullScreen`) ### Pickers and settings - Open Settings (`workbench.action.openSettings`) - Open Keyboard Shortcuts (`workbench.action.openGlobalKeybindings`) - Quick Open (`workbench.action.quickOpen`) - Show Command Palette (`workbench.action.showCommands`) - Select Color Theme (`workbench.action.selectTheme`) - Select File Icon Theme (`workbench.action.selectIconTheme`) - Select Product Icon Theme (`workbench.action.selectProductIconTheme`) Commands that edit files, format documents, run tasks or code, mutate source control, manage extensions or accounts, or come from extensions are intentionally excluded. ## Routing examples Expected to enter command review: - `toggle terminal` - `toggle panel` - `toggle sidebar` - `open settings` - `open keyboard shortcuts` - `open command palette` - `change VS Code theme` Expected to continue to chat: - `fix terminal toggling` - `format this document` - `run a task` - `change VS Code theme in this extension` ## Voice Mode follow-up The frontend displays and executes the selected command. Spoken `Running command X`

title: `send_to_terminal` progress message repeats first question when accepting all defaults in interactive commands
text:
## Bug

When an interactive command like `npm init` is run and the user accepts all defaults via the `askQuestions` carousel, every `send_to_terminal` progress message displays the first question's text (e.g. "Package name?") instead of the correct question for each prompt.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a chat session in default approvals mode
2. Ask the agent to run `npm init` in a terminal
3. The agent detects the interactive prompts and shows an `askQuestions` carousel with multiple questions (package name, version, description, entry point, etc.)
4. Accept all defaults by leaving every field empty and submitting the carousel
5. The agent sends each default answer via `send_to_terminal` (pressing Enter for each prompt)

## Expected Behavior

Each `send_to_terminal` progress message should show the corresponding question:

- Pressed `Enter` in terminal (replying to: Package name?)
- Pressed `Enter` in terminal (replying to: version?)
- Pressed `Enter` in terminal (replying to: description?)
- …

## Actual Behavior

Every progress message repeats the first question:

- Pressed `Enter` in terminal (replying to: Package name? (default: @xterm/xterm))
- Pressed `Enter` in terminal (replying to: Package name? (default: @xterm/xterm))
- Pressed `Enter` in terminal (replying to: Package name? (default: @xterm/xterm))
- …

## Cause

`_getQuestionContextForTerminal` matches the sent command text against carousel answer values to find the corresponding question. When all answers are identical (empty string for defaults), the loop iterates questions in order and always matches the first one.

## Fix

Use positional matching: count prior `send_to_terminal` tool invocations after the carousel in the response parts to determine the question index, rather than relying solely on answer-value matching.


---

title: Omni-chat folder routing
text: We should add support for multi-root routing in omni-chat - [ ] In a multi-root workspace, mention one folder explicitly in a prompt that creates a new session. Verify the session is created for that folder. - [ ] Repeat with a file or resource associated with another folder and with a prompt related to an existing folder-scoped session. Verify the strongest relevant folder is selected. We should add a **Change folder** action and an indicator of which folder was chosen as well --- Implemented and validated as part of #326698, which is now merged into main. Omni multi-root routing selects new-session folders from attached resources, explicit folder mentions, related-session metadata, or the configured default, and the destination UI shows the selected folder with a Change Folder action. Sharing media and context from merged PR #330024 for verification: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84913ee3-412a-4a1b-aea7-6ce01e6f1ac4 ## Description Omni already computed a workspace folder for new sessions, but its common new-session paths dispatched immediately. In multi-root workspaces this bypassed the destination panel, so users saw neither the selected folder nor a way to correct it before dispatch. ## Folder routing For a new session in a multi-root workspace, Omni chooses the folder in this order: 1. **Explicit folder mention:** matches the prompt against a workspace folder's display name or final path segment. Matching is case-insensitive, treats spaces, dots, underscores, and hyphens equivalently, recognizes “VS Code” as “vscode”, ignores names shorter than three characters, and prefers the longest match. 2. **Attached resource:** uses the workspace folder containing the first attached file or resource that maps into the workspace. 3. **Related session:** uses the first model-ranked result with confidence of at least 0.35 whose working directory or repository metadata maps to a workspace folder. Working directory is checked before repository path, and nested matches prefer the deepest folder. 4. **Default folder:** uses the last folder selected for a new Agent Host session when it is still part of the workspace. 5. **Final fallback:** uses the first workspace folder. The inferred destination is displayed as **New session in _folder_**. Its compact folder control opens an Agents-style searchable workspace menu anchored inside Omni. The menu lists every current workspace root with its full path and selected state, plus **Choose Folder…** for the native folder dialog and standalone working directories. Opening either picker pauses the countdown and closing or selecting resumes from the remaining time. Standalone folders use the existing Agent Host

title: Omni-chat folder routing
text: compact folder control opens an Agents-style searchable workspace menu anchored inside Omni. The menu lists every current workspace root with its full path and selected state, plus **Choose Folder…** for the native folder dialog and standalone working directories. Opening either picker pauses the countdown and closing or selecting resumes from the remaining time. Standalone folders use the existing Agent Host trust boundary: before spawning, workspace roots request workspace trust and external folders request resource trust for the selected URI. Declining aborts the agent invocation. The model picker renders in an adjacent transparent host above Omni, while the folder picker renders in a detached host to Omni's right. Neither picker resizes Omni. Omni's temporary local compose session also explicitly uses the Copilot Agent Host model pool, so the model picker shows the available targeted models instead of only **Auto**. ## Changes - Route multi-root new sessions through the correctable destination panel. - Show the inferred folder in a compact folder/chevron control before dispatch. - List all workspace roots in an anchored, searchable, accessible folder menu. - Add an Agents-style **Choose Folder…** action backed by the native folder dialog. - Preserve the existing Agent Host workspace/resource trust gate for selected folders. - Keep the model picker detached above Omni and open the folder picker to its right without resizing Omni. - Use the Agent Host model pool for Omni's routing composer. - Preserve automatic dispatch with the existing 10-second countdown and pause/resume behavior. - Keep single-root new sessions on the immediate path. - Add browser coverage for explicit folder inference, workspace selection, native folder selection, anchoring, filtering, and countdown behavior. Construct the Agents window workbench, which creates the main status bar service but does not render/create the main status bar part. 2. During startup, register experimental/default configuration that changes `workbench.modernUI`. 3. The status bar configuration listener calls `updateStyles()` before `Part.create()` has provided a container. 4. `assertReturnsDefined(this.getContainer())` throws `Assertion Failed: Argument is undefined or null.` A focused unit reproduction can invoke the configuration-driven style refresh once before and once after assigning the part element; only the latter should call `updateStyles()`.

text: ## Reproduction 1. Install and launch the latest [VS Code Insiders](https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/). 2. In PowerShell, create a local bare remote, a workspace clone, and one remote commit that the workspace has not pulled yet: ```powershell $root = Join-Path $env:TEMP "agent-turn-attribution-$([DateTimeOffset]::Now.ToUnixTimeSeconds())" $remote = Join-Path $root 'remote.git' $seed = Join-Path $root 'seed' $workspace = Join-Path $root 'workspace' New-Item -ItemType Directory $root | Out-Null git init --bare --initial-branch=main $remote git init -b main $seed 'base' | Set-Content (Join-Path $seed 'agent.txt') 'base' | Set-Content (Join-Path $seed 'external.txt') git -C $seed add agent.txt external.txt git -C $seed commit -m 'Initial files' git -C $seed remote add origin $remote git -C $seed push -u origin main git clone $remote $workspace Add-Content (Join-Path $seed 'external.txt') 'remote-change-to-pull' git -C $seed add external.txt git -C $seed commit -m 'Remote change to sync between agent turns' git -C $seed push code-insiders $workspace ``` At this point, `workspace` is one commit behind the remote `main` branch, but its working tree still contains the original `external.txt`. 3. Click **Sync Changes** (the circular-arrows action) and confirm if prompted. The sync performs a fast-forward pull. `external.txt` now contains `remote-change-to-pull`, while the first turn's change in `agent.txt` remains modified and uncommitted. 7. title: Status bar style refresh asserts before part creation in the Agents window
text:
The Agents window repeatedly logs this assertion during startup:

```text
2026-08-11 08:33:39.074 [error] Assertion Failed: Argument is `undefined` or `null`.: Error: Assertion Failed: Argument is `undefined` or `null`.
    at NE (.../out/vs/sessions/sessions.desktop.main.js:414:242)
    at Qi (.../out/vs/sessions/sessions.desktop.main.js:414:1216)
    at Mlt.updateStyles (.../out/vs/sessions/sessions.desktop.main.js:1414:72690)
    at Rxe.value (.../out/vs/sessions/sessions.desktop.main.js:1414:66143)
    ...
    at wSi.registerDefaultConfigurations (.../out/vs/sessions/sessions.desktop.main.js:462:74842)
    at R6e.processExperimentalSettings (.../out/vs/sessions/sessions.desktop.main.js:4790:35997)
```

I found five occurrences across four recent Agents window renderer logs.

The stack resolves to `StatusbarPart.updateStyles()`, specifically `assertReturnsDefined(this.getContainer())`. The Agents window creates the shared status bar service but intentionally does not create/render the status bar part. During startup, experimental/default configuration registration fires `onDidChangeConfiguration`; the listener added in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/329701 calls `this.updateStyles()` before a container exists.

The root fix appears to be making this configuration-driven refresh lifecycle-safe. For example, `updateStyles()` can return while `getContainer()` is undefined. Normal status bar styling remains covered because `Part.create()` invokes `updateStyles()` after assigning the container, and later configuration changes still refresh it.

Introducing commit: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/eb55ea151447d7607654d7046a18b37d3dca4704

(Written by Copilot)

title: Update ESLint to v10 (9.x reached end of life on 2026-08-06)
text:
ESLint v9.x reached end of life on 2026-08-06 and no longer receives fixes: https://eslint.org/blog/2026/02/eslint-v10.0.0-released/ (see also https://eslint.org/version-support/). The repo currently pins `eslint@^9.36.0`.

Findings from running the v10.8 migration locally (`node build/eslint.ts` passes cleanly on the full repo afterwards):

- `typescript-eslint` / `@typescript-eslint/utils` support ESLint 10 since 8.56, so the current `^8.45.0` only needs a bump.
- `@stylistic/eslint-plugin-ts` v2 is a legacy package: the ts-specific plugin was merged into the unified `@stylistic/eslint-plugin`, whose v5 line supports ESLint 10 (rule ids change from `@stylistic/ts/semi` to `@stylistic/semi`).
- `eslint-plugin-jsdoc` declares ESLint 10 support as of v63.
- `eslint-plugin-import` is still on ESLint ≤9: the latest release (2.32.0, June 2025) relies on `context` APIs removed in v10, but works wrapped with `fixupPluginRules()` from `@eslint/compat` (only `import/no-restricted-paths` is used here).
- `eslint-plugin-header` is unmaintained (last release Feb 2021, already needs the `meta.schema = false` workaround on v9) and also works wrapped with `fixupPluginRules()`.
- The local rules (`.eslint-plugin-local`, `extensions/copilot/.eslintplugin`) need a mechanical port off `context.getFilename()` / `context.getSourceCode()`, which were removed in v10.
- v10 turns `/* eslint-env */` comments into errors; there is one inert instance in `test/unit/electron/renderer.js` (`no-undef` is not enabled).
- The newer `typescript-eslint` / `eslint-plugin-jsdoc` versions report a handful of new `prefer-optional-chain` / `check-param-names` findings, all easy to fix.

I'd like to open a PR with the migration if the team is open to it.


---

A PR is welcome.

The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. --> - VS Code Version: 1.111.0 - OS Version: macOS 26.3.1 Steps to Reproduce: 1. Install an extension that registers a `CustomTextEditorProvider` for `.md` files (e.g. [MEO](https://github.com/vadimmelnicuk/meo)). 2. Set the custom editor as the default for `.md` files via `workbench.editorAssociations`. 3. Use **Global Search** (`Cmd+Shift+F` / `Ctrl+Shift+F`) to search for a term present in a `.md` file. 4. Click a search result entry to open/navigate to the match. Current Behavior: The custom editor (webview) opens for the `.md` file, but the clicked match position is never surfaced to the extension via any stable API. The result is that the custom editor has no reliable way to scroll to or highlight the clicked search match - a fundamental navigation expectation that works automatically for native text editors. Expected Behavior: When a Global Search result is clicked and the target file resolves to a Custom Editor, VS Code should surface the target match position to the extension via at least one of: - The `options` parameter of `resolveCustomTextEditor` (e.g. a `selection` or `range` field, analogous to `TextDocumentShowOptions.selection`). - A dedicated event or message posted to the webview containing the target range. - A stable public API (analogous to `vscode.window.activeTextEditor`) that exposes the requested scroll/reveal target for the active custom editor. Use Case: Extensions that replace the native text editor with a rich webview UI (WYSIWYG markdown editors, hex editors, visual data editors, notebook-like interfaces) need to respond to navigation requests from Global Search, Go to Definition, and similar VS Code surfaces. Without a range-passing mechanism,

title: Support Custom Protocol Links (e.g. zotero://) in Markdown Preview and Notebook

Instead, nothing happens or an error occurs. In the editor, I can use workarounds (such as selecting the link and using a custom extension), but in the markdown preview or notebook rendered view, there is no way to activate these links. **Use Case:** - Academic note-taking and research workflows often require quick access to local reference managers like Zotero. - Many users embed `zotero://` links in markdown notes, notebooks, or documentation to streamline their citation workflow. - Supporting clickable custom protocol links would greatly improve productivity and integration with local tools. **Feature Request:** - Allow custom protocol links (such as `zotero://`, `org-protocol://`, etc.) to be clickable in markdown preview and notebook rendered cells. - When clicked, VS Code should invoke the system protocol handler, similar to how browsers handle these links. - Optionally, provide a setting to enable/disable this feature for security reasons. **Additional Context:** - This feature is already supported in browsers and some local applications. - The lack of support in VS Code limits the integration of local reference managers and other custom tools. **My Attempts to Solve This (with AI Assistance):** I have tried to solve this problem with the help of GitHub Copilot (AI assistant). title: Outline drag-and-drop and layer visibility
text:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

While it's easy to manage and sort classes, private/public methods, and functions when a project is small, it becomes very difficult to keep all the context in mind as the codebase grows.

Currently, editor-folding is one tool we have for this(though it can be buggy, as I've reported in issue #310842). However, a much more convenient option already exists conceptually:  **OUTLINE** view.

Since VS Code already builds an AST to map out the document symbols, could we add some **drag-and-drop** functionality to the Outline panel? I would be incredibly powerful to rearrange classes, functions, and methods directly in the Outline view for languages that support this coding style (moving symbol in the Outline would automatically cut and paste the corresponding block in the editor).

Additionally, the Outline view currently expands fully every time a window or file loads, forcing me to manually collapse things to getan overview. It would be wonderful to introduce visibility toggles/layers, such as:

- `Classes Layer`/`Global Layer` - Collapses everything to show only top-level classes and global functions.
- `Method Layer` - Unfolds classes but keeps their internal methods/properties collapsed.

This would drastically improve code navigation and refactoring efficiency for large files.

title: Add a "Restart VS Code" button in the UI
text: <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ --> <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> <!-- Describe the feature you'd like. --> my request is comade with copilot since im not a native english speaker: Dear Microsoft / VS Code team, I would like to suggest adding a dedicated "Restart VS Code" button to the user interface. Currently, VS Code prompts users to restart after updates, but there is no easy, always-available way to manually trigger a full restart when needed. Having a restart option would be useful in cases where users want to ensure that the session is fully reset (e.g., after changing settings, extensions, or troubleshooting issues). Proposed solution Add a "Restart VS Code" button accessible from the UI A natural location could be under the Settings gear menu or the Command Palette The action should: Fully restart the application Preserve workspace state similar to normal restarts Why this would be helpful Ensures a clean session without leftover state Improves troubleshooting experience Provides consistency (restart is already prompted after updates) Makes the feature more discoverable for users who are not familiar with command-based workflows Additional context This is a small quality-of-life improvement, but it would be a nice and practical addition to the overall developer experience. --- From Command Palette (F1) you can run `Developer: Reload Window` > From Command Palette (F1) you can run `Developer: Reload Window` > Makes the feature more discoverable for users who are not familiar with command-based workflows This is exactly my point: more and more non‑power users are joining the community, and they often prefer UI-based interactions over command-based ones. Having a visible restart button would make this functionality more discoverable and accessible. Similar to how many users prefer the built-in Git UI over the terminal—even if the terminal is faster—because it lowers the barrier to entry. So this would be a small but valuable quality-of-life improvement. I feel like `Developer: Reload Window` serves the need already - for troubleshooting needs etc. For other scenarios, I'd be curious if you have more specifics on why you believe restart is needed - if there are bugs where state is not cleared when expected, we should fix those bugs. <!-- 6d457af9-96bd-47a8-a0e8-ecf120dfffc1 --> This feature request is now a candidate for our backlog. title: Start Menu pinned tile becomes invisible (transparent) after every auto-update on   Windows
text: not moved - ❌ Icon cache corruption — ie4uinit.exe -show alone doesn't always fix it; restarting StartMenuExperienceHost.exe does - ❌ Not specific to custom install path — the Code.VisualElementsManifest.xml and its referenced hash-named PNG folder are both intact post-update Possible root cause (AI-generated analysis): The root cause appears to be that VS Code's Inno Setup-based updater replaces Code.exe in-place during the update but does not call SHChangeNotify(SHCNE_ASSOCCHANGED, ...) or ie4uinit.exe -ClearIconCache after the file replacement. Windows' Start menu tile host process (StartMenuExperienceHost.exe) holds a cached rendering of the old Code.exe's icon resources in memory. Because the file path hasn't changed, Windows does not automatically invalidate the cache, and the stale cached data fails to map to the new binary's icon resources — resulting in the tile rendering nothing (invisible rather than a white fallback). Additionally, Code.VisualElementsManifest.xml references icon PNGs via a hash-named subfolder (e.g. <hash>\resources\app\resources\win32\code_150x150.png). Even though the manifest is updated to the new hash during installation, if StartMenuExperienceHost.exe has cached the manifest content from before the update, it may still reference the old (now-deleted) hash folder path. This would also cause a transparent tile. Suggested fix: In the Inno Setup installer script, add a post-install step: [Code] procedure CurStepChanged(CurStep: TSetupStep); begin if CurStep = ssPostInstall then SHChangeNotify(SHCNE_ASSOCCHANGED, SHCNF_IDLIST, 0, 0); end; Or in the [Run] section: [Run] Filename: "{cmd}"; Parameters: "/c ie4uinit.exe -ClearIconCache"; Flags: runhidden --- Thanks for creating this issue! It looks like you may be using an old version of VS Code; the latest stable release is 1.125.1. Please try upgrading to the latest version and checking whether this issue remains. Happy Coding!

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.121.0
- OS Version: macOS 26.5 (25F71)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Run the command `code --list-extensions`
2. Observe whether `github.copilot-chat` is present in the list

It seems to change from day-to-day or week-to-week. My theory is that with every new VS Code release, it ships with the most-up-to-date version of the extension bundled (and therefore is not present in the list), but the extension later receives an update over the bundled one (and becomes present in the list). I haven't thoroughly tested this theory, but it went from present to not present when I updated to the latest release (1.121.0). My guess is that it was introduced in 1.116.0, [when this extension became built-in](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_116#_github-copilot-is-now-builtin).

All I know is that I use that command to regularly sync [my VS Code extensions](https://github.com/jaminthorns/environment/blob/main/config/code/extensions/extensions), and `github.copilot-chat`'s presence in the list keeps changing. If my theory is correct, then I suppose that either:

- Any bundled extension should be excluded from `code --list-extensions`, regardless of whether it's been updated over the bundled version.
- All bundled extensions that are updatable should be included in `code --list-extensions`.

My guess is that the first would be easier to implement. Regardless, I'd just like for things to be consistent again.

---

This extension is now only present in the built-in list (`@builtin` search filter), so this no longer seems to be an issue.

title: fix: guard statusbar updateStyles against pre-create config change (fixes #330262)
text:
### Summary The status bar throws `Assertion Failed: Argument is undefined or null.` at startup on Mac, Windows and Linux (v1.133.0-insider, 326 users). `StatusbarPart.updateStyles()` calls `assertReturnsDefined(this.getContainer())`, but the newly-added configuration-change listener invokes `updateStyles()` while default configurations are still being registered — before the part's container (`this.parent`/`this.element`) exists — so the assertion fires. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#330262 Recommended reviewer: `@hawkticehurst` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`eb55ea15`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/eb55ea151447d7607654d7046a18b37d3dca4704) | | Author | `@hawkticehurst` | | PR | #329701 | | Message | Restore theme colors in Modern UI shell (#329701) | | Why | This commit added `this.updateStyles();` inside the `onDidChangeConfiguration` listener (statusbarPart.ts:228). That listener can fire during early startup — while `registerDefaultConfigurations` runs — before `Part.create()` sets `this.parent`, so `assertReturnsDefined(this.getContainer())` in `updateStyles()` receives `undefined` and throws. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Reg as ConfigurationRegistry participant Cfg as ConfigurationService participant Listener as StatusbarPart config listener participant Update as StatusbarPart.updateStyles participant Assert as assertReturnsDefined Reg->>Cfg: registerDefaultConfigurations (startup) Cfg->>Listener: onDidChangeConfiguration(MODERN_UI) Note over Listener: Root cause:
calls updateStyles() before
the part container exists Listener->>Update: updateStyles() Update->>Assert: assertReturnsDefined(getContainer()) Note over Assert: Error thrown:
Argument is undefined or null ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/statusbar/statusbarPart.ts` | crash site | L697 (from stack): `const container = assertReturnsDefined(this.getContainer());` | | `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/statusbar/statusbarPart.ts` | root cause | L225-L230: config listener calls `this.updateStyles()` unconditionally, before `create()` sets the container | | `src/vs/workbench/browser/part.ts` | context | L78-L85: `create()` sets `this.parent` then calls `updateStyles()`; `getContainer()` returns `this.parent` | ### Repro Steps The error is timing-dependent (fires only when a `MODERN_UI` default-configuration change is delivered before the status bar part is created during startup): 1. Launch VS Code (insider) so that experimental/default settings are registered during startup. 2. When `registerDefaultConfigurations` triggers an `onDidChangeConfiguration` event affecting `workbench.modernUI` before the workbench finishes creating the status bar part, `updateStyles()` runs with no container. 3. The assertion `Argument is undefined or null` is thrown from `assertReturnsDefined(this.getContainer())`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`statusbarPart.ts`): guard the newly-added `updateStyles()` call in the config-change listener with `if (this.element)`, so it only runs once the part has been created into a container. This fixes the problem at its source — the producer of the premature call — rather than at the crash site. The part already models the "not yet created" state explicitly elsewhere (e.g. `addEntry` checks `if (!this.element)` at L268), so this guard is consistent with existing lifecycle handling. When

title: fix: enrich truncated IPC object deserialize error (fixes #330263)
text: ### Summary Telemetry bucket `112c22ba-c8f9-9d2c-1f93-9f46466fb2ac` reports `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` thrown from `JSON.parse` inside `deserialize()` in `src/vs/base/parts/ipc/common/ipc.ts`, running in the agent host utility process (`agentHostMain.js`) while decoding an inbound IPC message delivered over a MessagePort. The message payload arrives truncated: the binary framing declares an object of N bytes, but fewer than N bytes are present, so `JSON.parse` on a partial/empty string fails with a context-free error that gives triage no way to see where the corruption happened. New in `1.133.0-insider` (`5a36a9c6`); not present in the `1.132.0` baseline (`df53daab`), matching the introduction of the Agent Host Protocol-over-IPC (MessagePort) plumbing. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#330263 Recommended reviewer: `@connor4312` ### Culprit Commit Ancestry could not be git-verified in this environment (blobless checkout, credentials stripped after checkout, so `git show <hash>` / `merge-base --is-ancestor` fail on on-demand object fetch). Within the `1.132.0` to `1.133.0-insider` regression window, the agent-host MessagePort transport that routes these IPC messages was introduced/reworked by: - `63a042819ddd4deaffd45ac84dc176d1f00bb49a` — "agentHost: use AHP for local connections" (routes local renderer traffic through the Agent Host Protocol over MessagePort) — Connor Peet (`@connor4312`). This is the most likely producer of the new truncated-frame path; the crash surfaces in the shared `deserialize()` utility rather than in the transport commit itself. ### Code Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[MessagePortMain message event - native Electron layer] -->|e.data possibly truncated| B[Protocol.onMessage ipc.mp.ts:21-26 VSBuffer.wrap or alloc 0] B --> C[ChannelServer.onRawMessage / onBuffer ipc.ts] C --> D[deserialize reader ipc.ts:304] D -->|DataType.Object| E[readIntVQL yields length N] E --> F[reader.read N - BufferReader.slice returns fewer than N bytes, NO error on underflow] F --> G[JSON.parse of partial string ipc.ts:322] G -->|SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input| H[telemetry bucket 112c22ba] ``` ### Affected Files - `src/vs/base/parts/ipc/common/ipc.ts` — `deserialize()` `DataType.Object` case (crash site and where the truncation first becomes observable). `BufferReader.read()` (lines 217-221) slices without erroring on underflow, so a short buffer silently yields a partial string. ### Repro Steps Deterministic user repro is not available (the truncation originates in the native MessagePort/utility-process boundary during agent host connect/disconnect, not in reproducible TS logic). Observed across Windows/Mac/Linux, 44 users, on `1.133.0-insider`. Conceptually: deliver a MessagePort frame to the agent host whose binary object header declares more bytes than the payload actually contains (e.g. a partial/racing frame during agent host teardown) and `deserialize` will attempt `JSON.parse` on a truncated string. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/base/parts/ipc/common/ipc.ts`, `deserialize()` `DataType.Object` case (the bypass site is `ipc.ts:322`, where

text: 44 users, on `1.133.0-insider`. Conceptually: deliver a MessagePort frame to the agent host whose binary object header declares more bytes than the payload actually contains (e.g. a partial/racing frame during agent host teardown) and `deserialize` will attempt `JSON.parse` on a truncated string. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/base/parts/ipc/common/ipc.ts`, `deserialize()` `DataType.Object` case (the bypass site is `ipc.ts:322`, where `reader.read(N)` can return fewer than N bytes without error because `BufferReader.read` slices without bounds-checking). Before calling `JSON.parse`, read the declared length N and the actual buffer, and if the buffer is shorter than declared, throw an enriched error naming the expected vs. received byte counts. This follows the cross-process-error principle: enrich the error with diagnostic context, do not swallow it. The error is still thrown and still reaches the telemetry pipeline, but the new bucket will carry actionable framing information (`expected N, received M`) instead of an opaque `Unexpected end of JSON input`, letting the transport owner see truncation is occurring and where. This does not add a `try/catch`, does not remove any `logService.error`, and does not coerce the bad value to a benign default — the corrupt frame is still rejected loudly. **Alternatives considered** - Wrap `JSON.parse` in `try/catch` and return `undefined`/empty object — rejected: swallows a real cross-process corruption, hides the producer, and breaks the telemetry signal that surfaced the bug. - Drop empty/short messages at the producer in `Protocol.onMessage` (`ipc.mp.ts`) — rejected as the primary fix: the true producer is the native MessagePort layer (not visible in TS), the exact truncation condition isn't reconstructable from source, and silently dropping frames there would mask the corruption for every channel without diagnostics. Enriching at the deserialization boundary keeps the signal while making it diagnosable for whichever transport is at fault. ### Recommended Owner `@connor4312` — authored the 1.133 Agent Host Protocol-over-MessagePort IPC plumbing (`63a042819dd`, "agentHost: use AHP for local connections") that introduced the new transport path in which this error appears. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/31504181345) · opus48 · 662.4 AIC · ⌖ 11.4 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests) <!-- gh-aw-agentic-workflow: errors-fix, engine: copilot, model: claude-opus-4.8, id: 31504181345, workflow_id: errors-fix, run: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/31504181345 --> <!-- gh-aw-workflow-id: errors-fix --> <!-- gh-aw-workflow-call-id: microsoft/vscode-engineering/errors-fix --> --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. title: fix: guard against disposed InstantiationService in Settings editor search (fixes #330277)

If the Settings editor is closed/disposed while one of those awaits is in flight, execution resumes and later calls `this.instantiationService.createInstance(SettingsTreeModel, ...)` on an already-disposed `InstantiationService`, which throws `InstantiationService has been disposed`. The throw escapes as an unhandled error (the search path `onSearchInputChanged → triggerSearch → onConfigUpdate`), producing the telemetry spike. Reported as pre-existing per the re-bucketing / pre-existing guidance. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User as User / config change participant Search as onSearchInputChanged / triggerSearch participant Cfg as onConfigUpdate (async) participant IS as InstantiationService participant Crash as createInstance User->>Search: change search / config Search->>Cfg: await onConfigUpdate() Note over Cfg: ⚠️ awaits gallery manifest fetches
editor disposed meanwhile Cfg->>IS: createInstance(SettingsTreeModel, ...) Note over IS: store already disposed IS->>Crash: 💥 _throwIfDisposed()
"InstantiationService has been disposed" ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiationService.ts` | crash site | L69 `_throwIfDisposed`, L119 `createInstance` (from stack) | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/preferences/browser/settingsEditor2.ts` | root cause (async re-entry after dispose) | L1457-L1670: `onConfigUpdate` awaits `getExperimentalExtensionToggleData`, `refreshInstalledExtensionsList`, `getManifest`, `createTocTreeForExtensionSettings`, then `this.instantiationService.createInstance(SettingsTreeModel, ...)` at L1670 | ### Repro Steps 1. Open the Settings editor with a query that engages the extension-toggle path (extensions with recommended settings, so gallery manifest fetches are triggered). 2. text: the pending awaits resolve, `onConfigUpdate` resumes and calls `createInstance` on the now-disposed `InstantiationService`, throwing. Because timing-dependent, slow networks / many recommended-setting extensions increase the likelihood. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/preferences/browser/settingsEditor2.ts` → `onConfigUpdate`): add a disposed-guard immediately after the final `await` point (`createTocTreeForExtensionSettings`, L1589) and before any synchronous service access. If `this._store.isDisposed` is true, the method returns early, so the disposed `InstantiationService` is never touched. This is a use-after-dispose async race, and the correct place for the guard is at the async re-entry boundary in the owning object (the consumer that resumed after dispose) — not inside `InstantiationService` (fix at the re-entry site, not the shared crash site, and never by widening/silencing the base service). The existing `logService.error` telemetry pipeline is untouched, and no `try/catch` is used to swallow the error. **Alternatives considered**: wrapping the `createInstance` call in `try/catch` — rejected because it would silence a real lifecycle bug at the crash site and hide the same use-after-dispose from every other consumer, instead of stopping the disposed object from being used. ### Recommended Owner `@rzhao271` — settings editor area owner and recent top contributor to `settingsEditor2.ts` (write access, active within the last 90 days). text:

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: Latest Stable (Version: 1.111.0)
- OS Version: macOS (Darwin arm64 25.3.0)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open VS Code and let it download an update automatically.
2. When "Update is ready, click to restart" appears, quit the app using Cmd+Q instead of restarting.
3. Reopen VS Code.

Expected:
VS Code should apply the downloaded update on next launch, or at least not re-download it.

Actual:
The update is not applied. When checking for updates again, VS Code downloads the same update again.

Notes:
In many other apps, once the update is downloaded, quitting and reopening applies it. At minimum, it should avoid downloading the same update twice (e.g., by verifying checksum).

---

Thanks for creating this issue! It looks like you may be using an old version of VS Code; the latest stable release is 1.112.0. Please try upgrading to the latest version and checking whether this issue remains.

Happy Coding!

This response isn’t really applicable to this issue. To reproduce and test the behavior, you actually need to be on an older version. Also, this bug has existed for quite a while-if it hasn’t been fixed, it’s very likely still present in the latest release.
Current version: 1.112.0

This was likely due to the https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/50200 issue in Electron which was present in VS Code 1.111.0 and 1.112.0. It has since been fixed in Electron and should not appear in current VS Code versions as we are on Electron 42.7.0.

@bilgilendir Please us know if this still occurs on latest VS Code releases.


I checked again, and the issue is still present @dmitrivMS 

After my feedback, VSCode added the download/update buttons in the top-right when an update is available. 
However, if VS Code is closed and reopened before clicking Update, pressing “Check for Updates” still starts the download from scratch.

So the update logic is still incomplete. 

Once an update has already been downloaded, VS Code should detect the existing downloaded package on the next launch and show the Update button directly, rather than downloading it again. 

Ideally, it should verify the downloaded package (e.g. via checksum/hash) and then proceed with the installation.

title: Commit message generation silently returns empty when response is prompt-filtered (RAI); custom instructions trigger it
text:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.60.0
- VS Code Version: 1.132.1
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.2 (arm64)
- Feature: SCM "Generate Commit Message" (sparkle button)
- Selected model: n/a — commit generation uses the internal utility model (gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18)

### Summary
When the commit-message request is blocked by the Responsible AI Service (`promptFiltered`, server returns HTTP 422), the sparkle button spins and then leaves the commit box **empty with no error, no notification, and no retry**.

Two problems:
1. **Silent failure (UX bug).** Any non-success response is swallowed. Unlike quota/rate-limit cases, prompt filtering shows nothing to the user.
2. **Custom instructions reliably trigger the RAI filter.** With `github.copilot.chat.commitMessageGeneration.instructions` set, generation is filtered every time; clearing the setting makes it succeed immediately — same repo, same staged diff. The instructions were plain Conventional-Commits text.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Add a few `commitMessageGeneration.instructions` entries (plain text, e.g. Conventional Commits rules).
2. Stage a change, click "Generate Commit Message".
3. Spinner runs, commit box stays empty. No error shown.
4. Clear the instructions array → generation succeeds on the identical diff.

### Logs (GitHub Copilot Chat)
```
[error] Server error: 422 Unprocessable Entity
ccreq:697a4fb1.copilotmd | promptFiltered | gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 | 612ms | [gitCommitMessageGenerator]
```
Clearing the instructions:
```
ccreq:464a4553.copilotmd | success | gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 | 992ms | [gitCommitMessageGenerator]
```

### Root cause (from open-source source)
In `src/extension/prompt/node/gitCommitMessageGenerator.ts`, only `QuotaExceeded`/`RateLimited` are surfaced; everything else (including prompt filtering) hits:
```ts
if (fetchResult.type !== ChatFetchResponseType.Success) {
    return undefined;
}
```
So a filtered response is indistinguishable from "no result".

### Suggestions
1. Surface a clear message when a commit-message request is prompt-filtered (like the RAI message in #253130), instead of silently returning empty.
2. Investigate why plain Conventional-Commits instruction text trips the RAI filter on the utility model (false positive).
3. Optionally retry/fallback to a larger model on filter, since users can't pick the commit-generation model.

### Workaround
Overriding the utility model via `chat.utilitySmallModel` (e.g. a newer model) avoids the false-positive filter and restores generation with instructions intact.

Related: #253130 (Meta: Responsible AI Service response blocking).


---

This issue is a duplicate of https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/253130. Please refer to that issue for updates and discussions. Feel free to open a new issue if you think this is a different problem.

title: Toolbar commands immediately close newly opened quick picks
text:
### Type of Bug

Regression

### Reproduction

1. Run a current VS Code Insiders build with the modern UI/style override and motion enabled.
2. Open Source Control.
3. Open a toolbar **More Actions...** menu for a repository.
4. Open **Branch** and invoke **Create Branch From...**.
5. Observe the quick pick.

This also reproduces with other commands invoked from workbench toolbars that open a quick pick. Invoking the same commands from the Command Center does not reproduce the problem.

### Expected Behavior

The command's quick pick remains open and focused.

### Actual Behavior

The Command Center/quick-pick surface briefly opens, then immediately closes and focus returns to the toolbar menu.

### Regression Details

The regression was introduced by c5f02db50896ef310d3c909628e651675644fcef ("Add open/close motion to button menus in workbench chrome", #325190).

Animated context views delay disposal for the close animation. During that interval, the closing toolbar menu remains focusable. Its existing mouse-out handling can focus the menu's `actions-container` after the command has opened and focused a quick pick. The quick pick then receives a blur event and closes.

The issue only appears when the context-view close animation is active, which explains why it reproduces on machines enrolled in the modern UI/style override but not necessarily on every machine running the same Insiders version.

### VS Code Version

Current VS Code Insiders (1.133 development cycle); regression is also present on the 1.132 release branch.

---

title: Allow users to specify which plugin to install in "Install Plugin from Source" command
text: The current implementation as of 1.132.0 let user enter a owner/repo, or git url or local path to install a plugin from source. This is not enough to determine which plugin to install when a remote git repo has more than one plugins in it. It is natural to host multiple plugins within one repository since the marketplace manifest spec supports declaring multiple plugins. Both Copilot CLI and Claude Code supports specifying which plugin to install in the installation command using the `plugin@marketplace` argument. --- This works for me. Make sure your repo is a marketplace.
